title: Drop the reform of company distributions
headline: Drop distributions reform. Costs £0.8bn in 2029-30.
description: From April 2028 the rules on taking value out of a company are tightened, so that profits taken as capital are taxed as dividends where that is the fairer treatment. The Treasury scores it at £0.8 billion a year. Switch this on to drop the reform.

baselinePolicy.text: The distributions framework is modernised from 6 April 2028 (Table 6.1 line 49).

source.quote: It will reduce opportunities for shareholders to structure how they take profits or other value out of a company to secure Capital Gains Tax treatment where dividend Income Tax treatment is more appropriate.

alreadyIncludes: The distributions framework is modernised from 6 April 2028 (Table 6.1 line 49).

lines.title: Distributions: Modernise the distributions framework from 6 April 2028

rawSource.note: Reversal: the Treasury’s costing with its sign reversed (positive scorecard values reduce borrowing; here receipts positive means more revenue).

caveats: The Treasury’s costing is on the OBR October 2026 forecast, the baseline used here. Effects before the start year are not applied: 2026-27 falls before any Budget of yours.

considerations.text: The Treasury’s scorecard figure is the certified direct costing for the measure, including the behavioural response the Treasury and OBR agreed; the Budget 2026 policy costings document gives the method.
